name: Heritage Square Market
tagline: Century-old pavilion gathering of heirloom orchardists & artisan cheesemakers
description: Nestled beneath the ironwork archways of the historic timber pavilion, Heritage Square Market is the cultural cornerstone of the regional slow-food movement. Founded over a century ago, it features multi-generational farm families bringing dew-drenched heritage produce, fresh-churned butter, sourdough boules, and cold-pressed cider.

vendors.name: Alder Creek Orchard
vendors.specialty: Crisp Honeycrisp, Roxbury Russet & Spiced Cider
vendors.bio: Cider makers since 1948, preserving heritage apple varieties.

vendors.name: Highland Valley Creamery
vendors.specialty: Raw Goat Chevre, Aged Tomme & Ash-Ripened Pyramids
vendors.bio: Pasture-foraged alpine dairy herd crafted into artisan wheels.

vendors.name: Timberline Foraging Co.
vendors.specialty: Golden Chanterelles, Black Morels & Pine Cone Honey
vendors.bio: Wild-foraged forest harvest gathered by licensed mycologists.

vendors.name: Copper Kettle Sourdough
vendors.bio: Stone-ground local organic grains baked in portable wood embers.

transportTip: Take the Central Tram to Civic Square station or park your bicycle at the complimentary valet along the north arcade.
parking: Dedicated underground garage with 2-hour free stamp; ample public racks.
seasonalityNote: Peak harvest arrivals hit stalls from 8:30 AM on Saturdays.

name: Coastal Harbor Wharf Market
tagline: Sea-breeze open-air stalls brimming with salt-marsh greens, berries & fresh catch
description: Set directly upon weathered cedar dock planks beside the fishing fleet, this maritime gathering celebrates the convergence of tide and soil. Farmers from coastal mist valleys bring sweet alpine strawberries and heirloom artichokes alongside cooperative day-boat line-caught wild fish.

vendors.name: Pacific Fog Farm
vendors.bio: Dry-farmed coastal flats nurtured by marine fog.

vendors.name: Salicornia Saltworks
vendors.specialty: Crisp Sea Beans, Flake Salt & Sea Fennel
vendors.bio: Hand-harvested coastal marsh edibles and solar-evaporated sea minerals.

vendors.name: Tide & Trough Apiaries
vendors.bio: Coastal wildflower honey extracted with raw centrifugal spinning.

transportTip: Ferry terminal Gate 3 is a 4-minute stroll; coastal bus line #18 stops at the pier entrance.
parking: Metered dockside parking or discounted pier garage validation with purchase.
seasonalityNote: Coastal berries run from early spring straight into late autumn.

name: Riverdale Greenbelt Commons
tagline: Riverside lawn community hub with biodynamic roots, raw milk & kid workshops
description: Spilling across lush riverside green lawns shaded by weeping willows, Riverdale is an idyllic Sunday ritual for families, chefs, and gardening enthusiasts. Vendors prioritize regenerative agriculture and minimal packaging.

vendors.name: Earthbound Willow Farm
vendors.bio: Holistic agriculture without chemical inputs for 30 seasons.

vendors.name: Meadowbrook Pastures
vendors.specialty: Grass-fed Raw Jersey Milk, Butter & Free-Range Yolks
vendors.bio: Heritage A2 Jersey cattle rotational grazed on clover pastures.

vendors.name: Wild Spring Herb Co.
vendors.specialty: Culinary Lavender, Wild Ramps & Fresh Tarragon
vendors.bio: Hand-cut culinary herbs and botanical teas.

transportTip: Direct access via Riverdale Greenway Bike Trail. Dedicated stroller & bike parking at south kiosk.
parking: Free meadow grass parking lot with electric vehicle charging stations.
seasonalityNote: Arrive before 10 AM on Sundays for coveted raw milk and spring ramps.

name: North Valley Harvest Sheds
tagline: Rustic timber sheds celebrating stone fruits, heirloom corn & small-batch olive pressings
description: Surrounded by rolling orchards and vine terraces, North Valley Harvest Sheds feels like stepping into a Mediterranean countryside feast. Timber roofs protect rows of sun-drenched stone fruits, hand-pressed varietal olive oils, and cured mountain sausages.

vendors.name: Sunridge Grove Olives
vendors.specialty: First Cold Press Mission Olive Oil & Cured Olives
vendors.bio: Centennial dry-farmed olive trees harvested each November.

vendors.name: Valley Orchard Estates
vendors.specialty: Cal Red Peaches, Mission Figs & Blenheim Apricots
vendors.bio: Tree-ripened fruit picked within 12 hours of display.

vendors.name: Oak & Iron Apiary
vendors.specialty: Creamed Wildflower Honey & Pure Beeswax Tapres
vendors.bio: Sustainably managed colonies supporting regional pollination.

transportTip: Valley Express Bus #42 drops off right in front of the main red barn.
parking: Large gravel lot with 200 free parking stalls.
seasonalityNote: Peach season peaks in July-August; olive pressings arrive late November.

name: Highland Hills Botanical Market
tagline: Elevated terrace market spotlighting microgreens, rare tubers & medicinal herb gardens
description: Perched on a cool mountain overlook with sweeping panoramic bay views, Highland Hills brings together experimental urban agronomists, permaculturists, and botanists. Renowned for nutrient-dense micro-greens, rare varieties of edible tubers, and culinary mushrooms.

vendors.name: Cloudline Micro-Farms
vendors.specialty: Radish & Pea Tendrils, Sunflower Shoots & Amaranth
vendors.bio: Vertical closed-loop hydro greens harvested with the root systems intact.

vendors.name: Spore & Root Collective
vendors.specialty: Lion's Mane, Reishi Powders & Oak Log Shiitake
vendors.bio: Grown on inoculated hardwood logs sourced from sustainable forest thinnings.

vendors.name: Ridgecrest Botanicals
vendors.specialty: Fermented Black Garlic, Herbal Elixirs & Shrub Vinegars
vendors.bio: Traditional Korean 60-day slow fermentation and whole food tonics.

transportTip: Ridge Cable Line stops at Vista Point; shuttle service runs hourly on Saturdays.
parking: Vista terrace parking lot with designated carpool stalls.
seasonalityNote: Cool highland air keeps crisp greens and brassicas sweet all summer long.

name: Old Town Plaza Farmers Exchange
tagline: Cobblestone evening market featuring artisan breads, heritage pork & heirloom tomatoes
description: On Thursday evenings and Sunday mornings, the 19th-century Spanish tile plaza transforms into an atmospheric community square. Lanterns hang from wrought-iron lampposts while live flamenco and acoustic jazz fill the evening air as locals pick up dinner ingredients.

vendors.name: Mission Valley Heirlooms
vendors.specialty: Brandywine, Cherokee Purple & Green Zebra Tomatoes
vendors.bio: Preserving open-pollinated seed varieties with unmatched vine flavor.

vendors.name: Oak Hollow Pastures
vendors.specialty: Pasture-Raised Berkshire Pork, Bacon & Sage Links
vendors.bio: Acorn-finished heritage hogs raised in open oak savannahs.

vendors.name: Old Hearth Bakery
vendors.bio: Natural levain naturally fermented with whole heritage wheat.

transportTip: Take the metro to Plaza Station; pedestrian walkway exits straight into the stalls.
parking: Municipal garage on San Carlos St — first 90 minutes free.
seasonalityNote: Thursday Twilight Market runs through late October.
